title: Most Formula One race wins, all time
hook: Who has won the most Formula One races?

source.name: Jolpica-F1 API (Ergast-compatible), season winners endpoint
source.terms: Jolpica-F1 data is published for free public use (Ergast-compatible community API; see https://github.com/jolpica/jolpica-f1 for terms). Cross-check text from Wikipedia is CC BY-SA 4.0.
source.notes: World Championship races only, 1950-2025 (2025 is the last complete season at retrieval). Includes the Indianapolis 500 rounds of 1950-1960, which counted toward the World Championship. Shared drives (1950s) credit the win to each listed driver, as the API records them. Cross-check vs Wikipedia (revid 1378639443): Lewis Hamilton API 105 at end 2025, 106 incl. 2026 races to date vs Wikipedia 106; Michael Schumacher API 91 at end 2025, 91 incl. 2026 races to date vs Wikipedia 91; Max Verstappen API 71 at end 2025, 72 incl. 2026 races to date vs Wikipedia 72; Sebastian Vettel API 53 at end 2025, 53 incl. 2026 races to date vs Wikipedia 53; Alain Prost API 51 at end 2025, 51 incl. 2026 races to date vs Wikipedia 51.

crossCheck.name: Wikipedia: List of Formula One Grand Prix winners

events.text: Nino Farina wins the first World Championship race (1950 British Grand Prix)
Juan Fangio passes Nino Farina for the all-time lead: 3 wins (1950 French Grand Prix)
Alberto Ascari passes Juan Fangio for the all-time lead: 7 wins (1952 Dutch Grand Prix)
Juan Fangio passes Alberto Ascari for the all-time lead: 14 wins (1955 Argentine Grand Prix)
Jim Clark passes Juan Fangio for the all-time lead: 25 wins (1968 South African Grand Prix)
Jackie Stewart passes Jim Clark for the all-time lead: 26 wins (1973 Dutch Grand Prix)
Alain Prost passes Jackie Stewart for the all-time lead: 28 wins (1987 Portuguese Grand Prix)
Alain Prost becomes the first driver to 50 wins (1993 British Grand Prix)
Michael Schumacher passes Alain Prost for the all-time lead: 52 wins (2001 Belgian Grand Prix)
Michael Schumacher becomes the first driver to 75 wins (2004 Spanish Grand Prix)
Lewis Hamilton passes Michael Schumacher for the all-time lead: 92 wins (2020 Portuguese Grand Prix)
Lewis Hamilton becomes the first driver to 100 wins (2021 Russian Grand Prix)
